elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its Affiliates against covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1 expressly requires Vendor to defend Customer and its Affiliates from and against any covered third-party claim.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its Affiliates against covered third-party claims and resulting losses.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1 requires Vendor to indemnify Customer and its Affiliates for the claims and all resulting damages, costs, expenses, and reasonable attorneys' fees.

elements.element: Covered claims must include allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(a) covers allegations that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(b) covers claims arising out of Vendor's breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: Covered claims must include data breaches caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(c) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor.

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(d) expressly covers Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnified party must provide prompt notice of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2 requires the indemnified party to give prompt written notice.

elements.element: The indemnifying party must control the defence of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2 gives the indemnifying party control of the defence.

elements.element: The indemnified party must provide reasonable cooperation in the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 20.2 requires reasonable cooperation from the indemnified party.

elements.element: Customer indemnity for Customer-provided content must be limited to third-party intellectual-property claims based on that content.
elements.evidence: Section 20.3 limits this category to third-party claims arising from content Customer provides in violation of a third party's intellectual-property rights.

elements.element: The only other permitted Customer indemnity category must be Customer's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section 20.3 makes its two listed categories exhaustive and identifies Customer's breach of Applicable Law as the only category in addition to Customer-provided infringing content.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party intellectual-property infringement claims concerning the Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 20.1(a) provides this Vendor IP indemnity and also includes a defence obligation.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no exclusion for modifications made by Customer.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by combinations with items not supplied or approved by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no combination exclusion.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims resulting from Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no exclusion for compliance with Customer specifications.

elements.element: The IP-infringement remedies must include procuring Customer's continued right to use the affected Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: No procure-right remedy appears in Sections 20.1-20.3.

elements.element: The IP-infringement remedies must include modifying the affected Services or Deliverables to be non-infringing.
elements.evidence: No modification remedy appears in Sections 20.1-20.3.

elements.element: The IP-infringement remedies must include replacing the affected Services or Deliverables with non-infringing substitutes.
elements.evidence: No replacement remedy appears in Sections 20.1-20.3.

elements.element: The IP-infringement remedies must include a refund remedy.
elements.evidence: No refund remedy appears in Sections 20.1-20.3.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnification liability must be subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: The rendered language does not state a three-times-annual-fees cap for Vendor indemnification liability.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the preferred position, including Vendor defence and indemnification, all four required triggers, the specified claim procedure, and an exhaustive limitation on Customer indemnity. The fallback is not independently complete because its exclusions, infringement remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap are absent. The redline is otherwise targeted and does not alter unrelated warranty language or introduce a contradiction.
